title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Post-construction clean
audience: Owners and account managers of post-construction cleaning businesses who quote handover cleans for builders, developers and property managers.
learningOutcomes: Write a handover offer with a clear promised standard, handover window, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk a builder or property manager carries at handover, and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only on time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'We clean new buildings' is a service. 'We clean the fit-out to a written handover checklist covering dust-off, glass, fittings, floors, bathrooms and kitchens, in one visit inside the handover window, and return within two working days for any item the principal contractor's inspection lists' is an offer. The builder buys a handover standard it can check, and a supplier that will not hold up the handover.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome, such as a handover-ready fit-out that passes the principal contractor's inspection; a defined handover window that matches the project program; the work the client must do, such as clearing the site of trade debris, providing water and power and confirming site access; the certainty you provide, such as a checklist and photos at completion; and the risk you carry, such as the return visit. Keep each part specific and checkable. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', last updated 1 August 2025). The research found no sourced standard for a handover clean, so write your checklist from your own experience and state it.

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make site access, induction and the handover sign-off simple. One named contact, a site induction completed before the first visit, and a single sign-off form reduce the decisions the builder has to make. Builders often accept a higher price for a cleaner who arrives when the site is ready and leaves it ready for inspection, because the client is paying for reliability on a tight timetable.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services. A written workmanship warranty is an optional extra that sits on top of those guarantees (business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', last updated 27 May 2025). Consumer Victoria explains that a service provider gets a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (last updated 13 October 2023), but that page sets no fix window, so write your own. Do not claim a result such as 'dust-free' unless you have tested it and can show the test. Check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measurable claim.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: No pricing source for post-construction cleaning was found in the research, so this lesson does not give a market rate. A vendor's make-good estimate for large Sydney commercial properties appears in the research, but it has no stated source and is not a per-square-metre or hourly rate, so it is not used here. Price from your own hours and cost, using BP-05 and HBM-12, and check the price against the scope the builder needs. Show one clear total and say whether GST is included (ACCC, last modified 15 July 2026). Stepped packages, such as a basic handover, a handover with glass and fittings, and a full make-good, can show the builder what each level adds (Jobber Academy, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). Label every figure in your own offer with its source, and do not borrow office or strata rates for a handover.

procedure: Write the handover outcome in one sentence a builder would repeat.
Set a handover window that matches the project program, and record how often you meet it.
List what the builder must do, such as clearing trade debris and providing water and power, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: a handover checklist with photos at completion.
Decide the return-visit promise and check that you can staff it within the time you state.
Price from your own hours and cost, then check the total and the scope before issuing the offer.

workedExamples.situation: A builder asks for a quote on a 180 m² office fit-out handover. The builder wants the space cleaned before the tenant's inspection and says it would like a fixed price. No price source was found for this work.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Write the offer and say what price basis you can support.
workedExamples.reasoning: The offer states the handover checklist, the window before the tenant inspection, the photos at completion, the return-visit promise, the exclusions (for example, removing trade debris unless the scope says it is included) and one total with GST status. The price is built from your own hours and cost. Illustrative figures only: 12 crew-hours at a cost of $55 an hour (illustrative) is $660, and with a 25 per cent target margin on price (illustrative) the price is $880. Because no post-construction source exists, these figures are for practice and must be replaced with your own records before any quote is issued.

commonErrors.error: Making a handover promise you cannot afford to honour
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the promise to a return visit inside the handover window, and write the window into the offer.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate, such as 'dust-free'
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the checklist standard you can show, and avoid absolute claims unless you have tested them.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. Whether a post-construction clean counts as construction work is not settled by the sources read for this lesson, so check the construction WHS rules and WorkSafe guidance for your state before you accept the work. Victoria has its own OHS Act and regulations, which this lesson did not check. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority.

qualityStandard: Every handover offer states the standard, handover window, client inputs, return-visit promise and GST status, and is checked against your own hours and cost. No unsourced price is used.
documentationEvidence: Written handover offer with scope, checklist, exclusions and window, the price basis, and the decision made.
summary: A handover offer promises a checkable standard inside a stated window, and it states its exclusions.
No post-construction pricing source was found, so price from your own hours and cost and label every figure.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a handover offer does the builder buy?
What should a return-visit promise be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

officialReferences.covers: Taken from the research file (team4-R-sol03-tactics, tactic 11): misleading statements about price are prohibited, which supports showing one all-in price with GST status. The page was not re-read for this variant. Publisher: ACCC.

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Supports: a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge. The page sets no fix-window length.
